stories.headline: Warriors withholding payments to Porzingis, sources say
stories.summary: The Golden State Warriors are not delivering semimonthly payments to veteran center Kristaps Porzingis on his $20 million salary, league sources told ESPN, ruling that the currently absent center is not rendering his services.
stories.body:
The Golden State Warriors are not delivering semimonthly payments to veteran center Kristaps Porzingis on his $20 million salary, league sources told ESPN, ruling that the currently absent center is not rendering his services.

General manager Mike Dunleavy and the Warriors' front office are still actively pursuing trade avenues utilizing Porzingis' contract even as the 31-year-old leans toward ending his NBA career.

For rival teams, absorbing Porzingis' near-expiring salary could either allow them to move a longer-term salary out to save money (plus clear a roster spot via buyout) or theoretically net a draft asset, depending on what the Warriors are willing to attach.

The Warriors have no current plans on voiding Porzingis' contract, team sources said, maintaining trade flexibility up until the Feb. 11 deadline. Porzingis is not disputing the lack of payments, league sources said.

Under different circumstances last season, the Miami Heat withheld payments for veteran guard Terry Rozier while he was under federal investigation in a gambling scandal but did spend the months leading up to the deadline exploring trade possibilities with his contract.

After battling an elongated health issue the past two seasons, Porzingis signed a two-year, $40 million extension with the Warriors this summer (only $3 million guaranteed in the second season). But on the eve of training camp, he called Dunleavy and stepped away from the team. The Warriors gave him some space initially but expected him to return to the facility and be around his teammates and the medical staff in his recovery, team sources said.

After a meeting with Dunleavy and Rick Celebrini, the team's lead medical decision-maker, in early October, the team sent out a statement declaring he would be around. It didn't last. Porzingis left the facility, hasn't returned and the organization shifted his official status from out with "general illness" (as they'd listed during his absences last season) to "not with team," a purposeful change.

This is no longer described as an excused absence for the center. In his absence, the Warriors have won five consecutive games after opening the season 0-3.

stories.headline: Champions League live updates: Real Madrid, Liverpool in action in early matches
stories.summary: Liverpool visit Fenerbahçe, Manchester City face RB Leipzig and Real Madrid travel to AEK Athens as the UEFA Champions League league phase continues Wednesday.
stories.body:
The Champions!

The UEFA Champions League continues Wednesday with another action-packed slate of league phase fixtures.

We kick things off with the early matches, in which Liverpool face Fenerbahçe and Real Madrid take on AEK Athens.

Later, Manchester City face off against RB Leipzig, while last season's runners-up Arsenal will look to continue their unbeaten European campaign in the Czech capital against Slavia Prague.

Elsewhere, Borussia Dortmund host Real Betis, Porto face off against Napoli and PSV Eindhoven take on Club Brugge. Finally, Lens welcome Como, while Viking face Sabah to round out the day's nine-match slate.

Enjoy all the latest updates, goals, highlights and analysis from across Europe!

stories.headline: Grading bold 2026 season predictions for all 30 MLB teams
stories.summary: It's time to see if what we said about each club going into the season was accurate or not -- and what it means for 2027.
stories.body:
Back in March, when the upcoming season looked bright for the Seattle Mariners and bleak for the Chicago White Sox -- oh, how wrong we were! -- I made a bold prediction for each MLB team as part of our season preview. I always try to make these reasonable and realistic, although some were a little more fearless than others.

Let's go back and grade each one of those predictions to see how I did -- and then spin things forward to 2027.

Chicago White Sox

The prediction: With Grant Taylor, look for the late innings to get better and the White Sox to improve by another 19 wins in 2026.

They didn't improve by 19 wins -- they improved by 24! And made the playoffs! Taylor was the most important player in the bullpen turnaround, going 7-3 with 10 saves and a 2.25 ERA and pitching 84 innings in various high-leverage roles. The bullpen improved from 30th in win probability added to 15th (while pitching the most innings in the majors).

Grade: A+

Looking ahead to 2027: Chicago cobbled together a solid bullpen, getting good work from journeymen like Sean Newcomb and Bryan Hudson. That won't necessarily be repeatable, so the White Sox will need more innings from their starters to alleviate some of the burden. In a best-case scenario, Hagen Smith and Noah Schultz will become key members of the rotation.

Detroit Tigers

The prediction: Kevin McGonigle posts an .825 OPS and 5.0 WAR to win American League Rookie of the Year.

McGonigle had an .806 OPS and 7.1 WAR via Baseball-Reference -- the eighth-highest total for a rookie position player since 1900 -- and will surely win top rookie honors. If we use FanGraphs, which was a little less generous with his defensive value, McGonigle comes in at 5.4 WAR.

Grade: A+

Looking ahead to 2027: McGonigle was an immediate star, riding a sweet swing, impeccable strike zone control (95 walks, 98th percentile chase rate) and positional value in splitting time between shortstop and third base -- all while adding 18 home runs. He might not be a shortstop in the long run, but he's such a well-rounded offensive player, with the potential for a little more power, that he should be one of the best players in the league for a long time.

Baltimore Orioles

The prediction: Pete Alonso leads the AL in RBIs -- becoming the first player to top both leagues.

Ding, ding, ding!

Grade: A+

Looking ahead to 2027: Alonso hit 43 home runs and drove in 113 runs. In case you were wondering, Mets first basemen hit 18 home runs and drove in 77 runs. The Mets worried about how Alonso might age, but he can still mash. Expect more of the same for at least another season.

Cincinnati Reds

The prediction: Chase Burns will live up to the hype and pitch 150 innings with a sub-3.00 ERA and more than 10 K's per nine.

Nailed it: 15-3, 2.86 ERA, 154 innings, 10.8 K's per nine. Don't blame Burns for Cincinnati's 75-87 season.

Grade: A+

Looking ahead to 2027: With a spectacular first full season, Burns should be ready to add another 25 innings or so -- he pitched seven innings just twice -- which could make him a top-five starter in the game.

Cleveland Guardians

The prediction: Parker Messick leads the team with 15 wins, becomes the first lefty Cleveland starter to make the All-Star team and finishes third in Rookie of the Year voting.

Well, Messick won only 12 games while Gavin Williams led the team with 14, but Messick was even better than expected: 12-9 with a 2.56 ERA, 193 strikeouts and 6.3 WAR -- arguably the best rookie season by a pitcher in Guardians history. He was an All-Star and should finish second behind McGonigle in rookie voting.

Grade: A

Looking ahead to 2027: Messick is your classic "knows how to pitch" lefty -- although that undersells his super-effective 94 mph four-seam fastball, which ranked as the fourth-most valuable pitch in baseball via Statcast's run value metric. (Jacob Misiorowski's and Cam Schlittler's four-seamers were first and second, respectively.) Impressively, Messick pitched 186 innings, so he has already shown he can handle a big workload.

Colorado Rockies

The prediction: Hunter Goodman becomes just the eighth primary catcher with a 40-homer season and makes the All-Star team again.

Check and check. Goodman hit 41 home runs while playing 99 of his 138 games behind the plate. He was a key part of a Rockies offense that improved from 597 runs to 752, the second-biggest year-to-year increase in the majors.

Grade: A

Looking ahead to 2027: The pitching is still a mess, so despite the development of homegrown hitters like Cole Carrigg and Kyle Karros, plus the emergence of TJ Rumfield, who led the National League in on-base percentage, the Rockies aren't close to contending. That probably means another offseason of Goodman trade rumors, even though he's under team control for three more seasons.

Houston Astros

The prediction: The Astros bounce back to win the AL West as Yordan Alvarez reaches 40 home runs for the first time in his career.

Look, this prediction worked out, but it's a little awkward to take full credit for it since the Astros won the division with an 81-81 record. Alvarez though? He bounced back from his injury-plagued 2025 and hit 42 home runs while capturing the batting title with a .316 average.

Grade: A-

Looking ahead to 2027: The Astros weren't a good team in 2026, getting outscored by 32 runs on the season, and it's hard to see how they'll get better in 2027. They'll be paying $55 million just for Jose Altuve (0.0 WAR in 2025) and Carlos Correa (1.3 WAR), plus the rotation is a mess. Of course, anything is possible in the AL West.

San Diego Padres

The prediction: Mason Miller will become just the second reliever ever with a sub-1.00 ERA and 100 strikeouts (Blake Treinen did it in 2018).

Almost got there. Miller had a 0.81 ERA as late as Aug. 24 but then had a 4.91 ERA over his final 13 appearances and finished with a 1.67 ERA and 129 strikeouts. It was the most strikeouts by a reliever since Josh Hader in 2019 and Miller's 16.59 strikeouts per nine innings was the fourth-highest total ever.

Grade: B+

Looking ahead to 2027: Assuming no lingering effects from his meltdown in the NLDS, Miller should once again be the top closer in the game.

Milwaukee Brewers

The prediction: Jackson Chourio has his breakout season, hitting .290 with 30 home runs and 5.0 WAR while making his first All-Star team.

So close. Chourio hit .291 with 25 home runs and 4.9 WAR -- but didn't play his first game until May 4 after starting the season on the injured list. That late start prevented him from making the All-Star team, but we'll still give this a high grade.

Grade: B+

Looking ahead to 2027: Chourio will be 23 years old, and there's still room for improvement as he's still below average in his walk and strikeout rates. If he can tighten up his swing-and-miss, his explosive tools will lead to even higher productivity, as he hit the ball harder in 2026 and hit it in the air more often.

Philadelphia Phillies

The prediction: Cristopher Sanchez will be great again ... but fellow lefty Jesus Luzardo will be even better.

This was a spicy prognostication and we almost nailed it, despite Sanchez having another huge season:

Sanchez: 18-7, 2.91 ERA, 8.1 WAR

Luzardo: 14-5, 2.86 ERA, 6.5 WAR

Luzardo was the Phillies' best pitcher in the second half and was red hot when he came down with shoulder inflammation in early September, not pitching again until the final day of the regular season. If he hadn't missed those starts, he might have matched Sanchez in WAR.

Grade: B+

Looking ahead to 2027: Luzardo has fanned 200-plus batters in three of the past four seasons, missing that mark only in 2024 when he made just 12 starts due to a stress reaction in his back. He has firmly established himself as a premier starter and should be primed for another big season, assuming there are no lingering issues with the shoulder.

Tampa Bay Rays

Prediction: Junior Caminero will tie Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s age-22 record with 48 home runs.

OK, this wasn't the boldest prediction considering Caminero hit 45 home runs in 2025, but only Eddie Mathews had two 40-homer seasons through age 22. Caminero didn't quite get to Guerrero, hitting 42, but he joins Mathews in that two-man club and will finish high in the MVP voting.

Grade: B

Looking ahead to 2027: Caminero had a better all-around offensive season than in 2025, improving his on-base percentage from .311 to .360. That improved selectivity is a scary thought for opposing pitchers. Not all 22-year-old hitters improve -- Bryce Harper had his best season at age 22; Guerrero has been up and down in his career since -- but it wouldn't be surprising to see Caminero push his way closer to a .400 OBP and .600 slugging percentage.

Boston Red Sox

The prediction: The Red Sox lead the AL in rotation ERA for the first time in 24 years.

Boston starters had a 3.92 ERA, which ranked fourth in the AL. Of course, this prediction was counting on Garrett Crochet to lead the way, but he made just six starts with a 6.30 ERA. The newcomers -- Sonny Gray, Ranger Suarez and Payton Tolle -- were outstanding. Brayan Bello was not. Jake Bennett was a pleasant surprise.

Grade: B-

Looking ahead to 2027: Crochet made it back for an ill-advised appearance in the wild-card series, so he should be ready. Gray has a $30 million mutual option, so he may or may not be back. Bello pitched much better as a bulk guy out of the bullpen but should be back in the rotation. Trades have depleted the depth, but if Crochet can tee it up 30 times, this should once again be a top rotation.

Athletics

The prediction: Leo De Vries and Gage Jump will both debut in 2026.

Hey, 1-for-2 in baseball is a great average. De Vries entered 2026 as ESPN's No. 11 overall prospect. He spent the entire season as a 19-year-old in Double-A and held that status, climbing up to No. 4 in Kiley McDaniel's updated August rankings, after hitting .290/.378/.458. He might have been in line for a September call-up but injured his shoulder and eventually underwent surgery to repair a labrum tear. Jump made 21 starts for the A's, going 6-11 with a 5.47 ERA.

Grade: C+

Looking ahead to 2027: De Vries' surgery will keep him out until May or so and probably delay his progress to the majors. Prior to the injury, he was projected as a better defensive shortstop than Jacob Wilson, but De Vries will have to show the arm strength is still there. Jump should be in the rotation, looking to refine his control and a six-pitch repertoire that plays off a 96 mph fastball.

Kansas City Royals

The prediction: Bobby Witt Jr. posts 9.5 WAR, breaking the club record of 9.4 he shares with George Brett. He belts 92 extra-base hits, which would be a record for a shortstop. And he wins AL MVP.

First off, that's three predictions rolled into one giant "Witt is going to have an absolute monster season" forecast. Second, Baseball-Reference now lists Witt's 2024 WAR as 9.6, so he's now above Brett. Third, Witt was great -- 6.7 WAR, which ranked third among AL position players -- but not "92 extra-base hits" great (he had 52 while missing 19 games).

Grade: C

Looking ahead to 2027: For now, Witt's .332 average that drove his best season in 2024 remains an outlier, as he's followed that up with seasons of .295 and .281, with less over-the-fence power as well. Some of this is batted ball luck -- his Statcast expected average in 2024 was .309 compared to .302 in 2026 -- but he also began this past season with a 27-game homerless streak. At the minimum, he's one of the best all-around players in the game. If he can get back to hitting 30 home runs, maybe he'll get that MVP trophy.

Arizona Diamondbacks

The prediction: Geraldo Perdomo proves his 2025 wasn't a fluke, hitting .300 while scoring and driving in 100 runs.

Perdomo hit .290 with 20 home runs, 100 RBIs and 98 runs to finish fourth in the MVP voting last season but fell off to .262/.370/.377 with nine home runs, 59 RBIs and 75 runs this year. With 5.1 WAR, it was still an excellent season, confirming Perdomo as one of MLB's top shortstops.

Grade: C

Looking ahead to 2027: Perdomo's hard-hit rate was identical to 2025, but he didn't barrel up quite as many baseballs. Don't expect 20 home runs, but his ability to get on base and play excellent defense (98th percentile in range via Statcast) will make him a valuable player once again.

Texas Rangers

The prediction: Nathan Eovaldi and Jacob deGrom both pitch 170 innings and post sub-3.00 ERAs.

Well, the two vets did have nearly identical seasons, but the prediction was overly optimistic. Eovaldi went 11-10 with a 4.20 ERA, deGrom 11-11 with a 4.20 ERA (although a 3.11 FIP). Eovaldi had a stint on the IL and pitched 145 innings; deGrom made his 31 starts but pitched just 162 innings as he became a five-and-dive guy.

Grade: C

Looking ahead to 2027: Hard to believe, but deGrom is already entering the final season of that five-year deal he signed (not including a $20 million team option for 2028). He'll be making $37 million. Eovaldi will be in the final year of his three-year contract. The Rangers will probably be happy to get 54 starts out of this pair again, and it's reasonable to expect both to lower those ERAs if they stay healthy.

Los Angeles Dodgers

The prediction: The Dodgers take on a new challenge after winning back-to-back titles and crush the regular season, winning 110 games.

It easy to say the Dodgers didn't push to be great, but there were on-field reasons why they didn't win 110 games: Kyle Tucker was a flop, Freddie Freeman had a down season (he hit just one home run after the All-Star break), Mookie Betts didn't hit much until September and Will Smith played just 73 games. Not to mention Shohei Ohtani, Tyler Glasnow and Blake Snell combined for just 36 starts. All that happened and the Dodgers still won 100 games.

Grade: C

Looking ahead to 2027: More innings from Ohtani, Glasnow and Snell will help and a better year from Tucker and the likely emergence of Josue De Paula as an immediate offensive force will also help cover the age-related concerns with Freeman and Betts. Once again, 100 wins almost feels like a slam dunk.

Los Angeles Angels

The prediction: Mike Trout plays 140 games for the first time since 2018 (including 100 in center field), hits 35 home runs and finishes in the top 10 of MVP voting.

Hey, he played 142 games! And 109 in center! Trout finished seventh in the majors in on-base percentage, but he hit just 22 home runs, including four in 64 games in the second half. His 4.1 WAR was his most since 2022, but his days as a top-10 MVP finisher appear over.

Grade: C

Looking ahead to 2027: Trout's first half was certainly encouraging, but the lack of power in the second half was hopefully just an anomaly. The Angels should still find a better defensive center fielder, but if staying in center helps keep Trout motivated and stay in the lineup, they'll probably live with his defense.

Atlanta Braves

The prediction: The Braves will score 100 more runs than in 2025.

The Braves did improve on offense -- but by 18 runs, not 100. Austin Riley had his worst season, shortstop was still a big problem and Ronald Acuna Jr. was good but not great. The big gains came from Michael Harris II, plus Drake Baldwin getting more plate appearances.

Grade: C-

Looking ahead to 2027: The Braves need to find a solution for shortstop, and now Riley, who is signed through 2032, looks like a potential long-term problem as well. Acuna's MVP season of 2023 is starting to look like the distant past. They're probably a league-average offense again unless Acuna stays on the field and reignites.

Washington Nationals

The prediction: They lose more games than the Rockies and finish with the worst record in the majors. CJ Abrams and Zack Littell are traded.

From the list of things we did not see happening: The Nationals finishing third in the majors in runs scored. They scored more runs than the Dodgers! The pitching, while still not great, was a little better and the Nationals finished a respectable 77-85, their best record since their World Series year of 2019. Abrams wasn't traded but Luis Garcia Jr. and Curtis Mead were, and while Littell wasn't traded either (he was released instead), Foster Griffin was, so we got the part about the Nationals trading players away at the deadline correct. But that won't salvage this grade.

Grade: C-

Looking ahead to 2027: Washington needs to replace the offense Garcia and Mead provided and still needs help in the rotation, too. Connelly Early, acquired for Mead, should be part of that solution if healthy, but president of baseball operations Paul Toboni might need to dip into free agency to cobble together the rotation.

New York Yankees

The prediction: The Yankees become the fifth team with five 30-homer players as Aaron Judge, Ben Rice, Jazz Chisholm Jr., Trent Grisham and Cody Bellinger all get there. They lead the majors with 290 home runs.

Rice, who hit 41 home runs this season, was not just the club's only 30-homer hitter -- he was also the only one to even reach 20. Not including 2020, the last time the Yankees didn't have at least two 20-homer guys was 2013. They did manage to finish second in the majors with 223 home runs.

Grade: D+

Looking ahead to 2027: Death, taxes and Yankees hitting home runs. They've finished first or second in the AL in home runs in eight of the past 10 seasons. Judge played just 66 games in 2026, plus they'll get a full season from trade acquisition Luis Garcia Jr., who hit 30 home runs between the Nationals and Yankees. Spencer Jones likely takes over in center field and he can hit 30 if he makes enough contact.

Chicago Cubs

The prediction: Michael Busch becomes just the second Cubs first baseman with a 40-homer season.

If only the prediction had been Pete Crow-Armstrong hitting 45 home runs and having perhaps the best all-around season in Cubs history. That would have been bold. Busch, who hit 34 home runs while playing mostly against just right-handers in 2025, played every day in 2026 but finished with 20 home runs.

Grade: D

Looking ahead to 2027: Busch still did some good things, such as drawing 92 walks to give him a .352 OBP, so we're not giving this a complete failing grade. He even hit better against lefties than righties. He had just three home runs through 45 games, so look for a better start in 2027 and a 30-homer season.

New York Mets

The prediction: Francisco Alvarez will hit 30 home runs, make the All-Star team and be the best offensive catcher in the NL.

Alvarez, who hit 25 home runs as a 21-year-old rookie in 2023, finished at .233/.311/.399 with 16 home runs. He was not an All-Star and ranked eighth in wRC+ among NL catchers with at least 300 plate appearances.

Grade: D

Looking ahead to 2027: Alvarez got hurt once again, suffering a torn meniscus in his right knee (although he missed only a month). He had a .710 OPS before the injury and a .710 OPS after returning, so that didn't seem to affect his production. He was hitting well through mid-August but hit just .188 with three home runs in his final 32 games. He'll still be just 25 years old in 2027, but it's becoming less likely he pops big.

Minnesota Twins

The prediction: The Twins trade Joe Ryan to the Brewers.

Ryan was one of the few Twins veterans to survive the trade deadline purge of 2025, so with the Twins viewed as unlikely contenders heading into 2026, he seemed like a reasonable trade candidate. Alas, in the muddy AL, the Twins were just four games back in the AL Central at the deadline and one game back of the final wild card. They kept Ryan, who then got hurt the day after the deadline and missed a month as the Twins faded out of the race. (The Brewers did trade for a starting pitcher, acquiring Dustin May from the Cardinals, so at least we got that part right.)

Grade: D

Looking ahead to 2027: Ryan has a $13 million mutual option for 2027 (although he's not eligible to become a free agent until after the 2027 season). He, Bailey Ober and Dean Kremer are all eligible for free agency then, so it's possible the Twins look to trade one of those guys rather than risk losing all three -- and Ryan will make the most money and bring back the best return if they do look to deal.

Pittsburgh Pirates

The prediction: Paul Skenes wins the Cy Young Award, Konnor Griffin and Bubba Chandler finish 1-2 in the Rookie of the Year voting and the Pirates win the final wild card with 83 wins.

Nope, nope and nope -- although the Pirates did win 82 games, so this isn't quite a complete failing grade. We won't dig into Skenes' numbers here, but it was a combination of regression -- and certainly regression in velocity -- and bad luck as the Pirates weren't a good defensive team in 2026 (he still ranked 14th in FanGraphs pitching WAR). Griffin and Chandler certainly showed off their high-ceiling talent. Suffice it to say: If this trio had met preseason expectations, the Pirates win more than 83 games and likely grab a wild card.

Grade: D-

Looking ahead to 2027: Things are ... dare we say ... going in the right direction? Better seasons from Skenes, Griffin and Chandler should make the Pirates a strong playoff contender, at least if the offense doesn't regress much after improving 184 runs from 2025 to 2026.

San Francisco Giants

The prediction: Logan Webb leads the NL with 18 wins.

The guess here was that after leading the NL three straight years in innings, all Webb needed was better run support to surpass his previous high of 15 wins. A swing-and-miss. The Giants' offense didn't get any better, plus Webb missed three weeks in May with bursitis in his knee (which snapped a streak of 156 consecutive starts) and then his season ended in mid-September due to a blister. He pitched just 160 innings and posted a 4.31 ERA, his worst since his breakout in 2021, while finishing with eight wins.

Grade: F

Looking ahead to 2027: Webb had fanned 26.2% of the batters he faced in 2025 but fell off to 20.1% this past season. That's not necessarily a crisis since it's close to his rates in 2022 and 2024, but he'll be 30 years old next year with that string of 200-inning seasons on his right arm. Webb said the knee didn't bother him after receiving a cortisone injection, so hopefully a healthy knee is all he needs to get back to his usual workload and performance.

Miami Marlins

The prediction: The Marlins will trade Sandy Alcantara ... to the A's.

Well, sometimes you're more Nuke LaLoosh than Luke Littler when throwing darts. The theory here was (A) the A's would be competitive and would need pitching help at the deadline; and (B) the Marlins would not be competitive and trade Alcantara. This is not what happened and Alcantara remained with the Marlins, who finished 80-82.

Grade: F

Looking ahead to 2027: The Marlins will pick up Alcantara's $21 million option for 2027, the final year on his contract. Coming off a year in which he led the majors in games started and innings pitched, his ability to pitch deep into games is especially important for an organization that has had trouble keeping starters healthy. With the Marlins harboring playoff hopes after an 80-win season, the best bet now is to keep him as the veteran leader on the staff.

St. Louis Cardinals

The prediction: After working with Nolan Arenado's personal hitting instructor in the offseason, Nolan Gorman will hit .250 with 35 home runs.

If we substitute "Jordan Walker" for "Nolan Gorman" this would have been a first-rate prediction. Alas, while Gorman did get one final opportunity, it did not work out: He hit .184 with nine home runs and spent most of the summer in the minors.

Grade: F

Looking ahead to 2027: Gorman has over 500 games in the majors now, but it just hasn't clicked following a promising 2023 season in which he hit 27 home runs. The Cardinals will be searching for a new third baseman for 2027.

Seattle Mariners

The prediction: Julio Rodriguez avoids his usual slow start, hits .290 with 40 home runs, reaches 8 WAR and finishes third in the MVP voting.

There was some logic here: Rodriguez hit .290/.341/.560 with 18 home runs in 65 games in the second half in 2025. All he had to do was perform at that level for six months. He did not. He had one good month -- he hit .274 with 10 home runs in May -- but the rest of his season was a disappointment as he finished hitting .247/.307/.401 with 22 home runs and 2.8 WAR.

Grade: F

Looking ahead to 2027: J-Rod's on-base percentage has declined four straight seasons since his rookie season. He lacked focus at times and his frustrations at the plate seemed to carry over to his defense, where his metrics declined. His chase rate was a career worst 38.6%, which ranked 125th out of 134 qualified regulars. The swing decisions need to improve, but after five seasons in the majors, that's becoming less likely.

Toronto Blue Jays

The prediction: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. hits .335 and joins John Olerud as the only Jays hitter to win a batting title.

As bad as the Rodriguez prediction was, this one was even worse. Guerrero hit an empty .260 with just nine home runs, including one at home.

Grade: F

Looking ahead to 2027: No player will be under the spotlight more in 2027 than Guerrero, who will be entering the second year of his 14-year, $500 million contract. While he apologized for his comments late in the season when he said he was getting paid for what he had done, not what he would do in the future, that contract already looks like a potential franchise-altering disaster for the Jays if he doesn't turn it around.

stories.headline: WNBA Finals saw surge in attendance and record ratings
stories.summary: The WNBA Finals was the most watched since 1999 with an average of 1.88 million people viewing the seven-game series that Golden State won over Atlanta in a decisive
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- The WNBA Finals were the most watched since 1999 with an average of 1.88 million people viewing the series that Golden State won over Atlanta in a decisive Game 7.

That game averaged 3.3 million viewers, making it the most watched WNBA postseason game ever. It was up 128% from last season's clinching game between Las Vegas and Phoenix that the Aces won.

All seven games in the series were sold out, including Game 6, which was played at 12:30 p.m. EDT.

The Finals capped the WNBA's most-watched postseason since its inaugural season in 1997, averaging 1.49 million viewers, up 27% from last year.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal want Atlético Madrid winger
stories.summary: Arsenal are keeping tabs on Atlético Madrid winger Álex Baena. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Atlético Madrid winger Álex Baena has caught the eye of Arsenal, while Juventus are weighing up approaches for Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko and AS Monaco forward Folarin Balogun. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Arsenal are keeping tabs on Atlético Madrid winger Álex Baena, TEAMtalk reports. An offer worth €80 million is expected to be required to secure the 25-year-old's transfer, as the Gunners explore the market for a top option to play on the left flank. The Premier League side could face competition from Bayern Munich for Baena, who has scored five goals and provided three assists in 11 LaLiga matches this season. Arsenal could raise funds for this with the exit of midfielder Martín Zubimendi, amid interest from Real Madrid and Barcelona, according to TEAMtalk. The 27-year-old has struggled to start regularly since the arrival of Bruno Guimarães and the Gunners would want a fee around the €60 million that they parted with to land him from Real Sociedad in July 2025.

- Juventus are weighing up approaches for Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko and AS Monaco forward Folarin Balogun, with plans to land a striker in January, Calciomercato reports. The Serie A club are keen to acquire a physical front man in the next transfer window, when they are expected to have around €100 million available to reinforce their squad. Šeško, 23, hasn't featured for United since Sept. 16 in the EFL Cup against Brighton due to injury, while a move for 25-year-old Balogun could be possible after Monaco accepted an initial €40 million offer from Everton in the summer before the deal fell through.

- Manchester United are considering a move for Al Ahli striker Ivan Toney as they prioritize adding depth at the No. 9 position, according to Football Insider. stories.headline: Major hockey worlds sponsors monitoring Russia's inclusion
stories.summary: The pressure on the International Ice Hockey Federation has grown as two major sponsors of the men's world championship said they would review their involvement if Russia takes part.
stories.body:
DUESSELDORF, Germany -- The pressure on the International Ice Hockey Federation grew Wednesday as two major sponsors of the men's world championship said they would review their involvement if Russia takes part.

The tournament's main sponsor, automaker Skoda, said it will "reassess" its involvement if Russia plays, and another longtime backer, Strauss, said it would refuse to have its logo shown.

A Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling last week obliged the IIHF to lift its exclusion of Russian national teams, which had been in place since 2022 over the war in Ukraine.

The IIHF said Wednesday that the impact of the ruling had been "significantly underestimated" and that it was still deciding how to react.

Almost half of the 16 nations in the men's championship in Germany in May are refusing to play Russia. The Canadian government also says it will not allow Russia to compete at the world junior championship there starting next month.

"We do not support the Court of Arbitration for Sport's decision regarding the participation of Russian national teams in IIHF competitions," the Czechia-based automaker, which is part of Germany's Volkswagen Group, said in a statement Wednesday. "With Russia's aggression continuing, we believe the Russian national team's return to the world championship is incompatible with the values we have consistently upheld.

"If the Russian national team takes part in the tournament, we will reassess our involvement in the tournament and take further action. We are actively monitoring the situation, remain in close contact with our partners and are confident that a constructive solution can be found."

Skoda has been a tournament sponsor for more than 30 years.

The CEO of Strauss, which makes work clothing and equipment, said his company could withdraw as a sponsor if Russia plays.

"We have been a partner of the Ice Hockey World Championship for many years and value our collaboration with the IIHF," Henning Strauss said in a statement. "Should Russia's national team participate in the 2027 World Championship in Germany as a result of the CAS ruling, we will forgo all logo exposure associated with the tournament. We are also considering withdrawing as a sponsor."

Other sponsors have been critical of Russia's return. Nokian Tyres said it would end its backing if Russia takes part, and furniture maker AJ Products, a tournament sponsor since 1989, said Monday that it would ask for its logo not to be shown.

"The IIHF is aware of the recent statements made from key stakeholders regarding this decision and is carefully analyzing the scenarios around CAS's ruling," the federation said. "As presented to the CAS, the immediate reintegration of Russian teams presents significant practical and sporting challenges, including visa and entry requirements, security provisions, logistical constraints and consequences for competition formats, all compounded by the limited time available, with some events only weeks away.

"The global impact of the decision made by the CAS Panel and the challenges it creates for all involved were significantly underestimated."

Finland, Sweden, Czechia, Norway, Denmark and Latvia have said they will play the tournament but not games against Russia in a growing boycott since Finland declared its position Monday.

The Austrian federation became the seventh to join late Tuesday when its CEO Alexander Helwig told broadcaster ORF that "as of now, we would certainly not play against Russia" as part of broader European opposition.

Russian Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyarev said in a statement via the Tass news agency Tuesday that he expected his country to be awarded wins if other nations forfeit games and that Russia would send information to the International Olympic Committee about potential boycotts and the conduct of host nations.

stories.headline: Charles Leclerc to miss Brazilian Grand Prix media duty due to birth of baby
stories.summary: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc will miss media duties ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix following the birth of his first child.
stories.body:
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc will miss media duties ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix following the birth of his first child.

The Monagesque driver announced on Instagram that his wife Alexandra gave birth to their daughter Bianca on Tuesday.

Leclerc had been scheduled to answer questions from the press on Thursday but has been allowed extra time at home with his family in Monaco.

The 29-year-old's absence means he will not address criticism from team-mate Lewis Hamilton following their tussle in the Mexico Grand Prix last weekend.

Hamilton accused Leclerc of working against him after he tried to overtake the British driver during the first lap when the pair were in front, opening the door for Max Verstappen to win the race.

"We have to have some serious talks behind the scenes for sure," Hamilton said.

- Kimi Antonelli to shun number one on car for 2027 season as new F1 champion wants to 'stay humble'

- Lewis Hamilton: Watching successor Kimi Antonelli win title 'highlight of my year'

- George Russell admits his F1 season had 'more bad days than good' following Kimi Antonelli championship triumph

"We don't have rules of engagement and, whether or not that will change anything from Charles' side, I don't know. Something needs to change for sure.

"I think it's a mentality thing. It's like, 'Do or die. Either I win or none of us do,' and it shouldn't be that."

The spat was met with frustration by Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur, who told Sky Sports: "I think it's just a matter of respect. Honestly, it's difficult to digest for me to give up a win like this."

stories.headline: Chris Fagan to join the Blues as director of coaching in 2027
stories.summary: Triple premeirship coach Chris Fagan has made the call on his AFL future, joining Carlton as their director of coaching for 2027.
stories.body:
Triple premeirship coach Chris Fagan has made the call on his AFL future, joining Carlton as their director of coaching for 2027.

The 65-year-old stepped down as Brisbane's senior coach after the club's 2026 premiership win -- it's third in a row -- with an aim to return closer to family.

Announced by the Blues on Saturday morning, Fagan will oversee a matchday role and begin mentoring the coaching panel to "establish development pathways for the coaches and help drive an elite, sustainable football program".

Fagan said he was looking forward to making a "real impact" at the Blues.

"While I loved my 10 years as a Senior Coach, this is a role I am passionate about and where I know I can have a real impact in this next phase of my football career," Fagan said in a statement.

"Supporting people to get the absolute best out of themselves is what I love most about football, so the chance to now be able to do that on a full-time basis is incredibly exciting. I can't wait to connect with each person in the football department, and in particular work closely with Josh to help every coach and player be the best Carlton person they can possibly be.

"In all my conversations with [the club] before accepting the role, what resonated strongly was how aligned they were on how to make Carlton a great football club. They shared a clear vision of evolving Carlton into a club that can contend but most importantly, they understand there is still significant work to do to get there.

"To have the senior leadership of a football club share such clarity in their direction, combined with a role that gives me genuine purpose, makes joining Carlton an opportunity too good to pass up."

Meanwhile Carlton's GM of Football Chris Davies said the appointment was an important one to support first-time senior coach Josh Fraser.

"We want to build our football club around good people and they do not come any better than Chris Fagan," Davies said.

"Few in the game have his wealth of experience and ability to connect with and get the best out of those around him. Most importantly, he is a proven winner who knows what it takes to build a consistently high-performing environment.

"Chris and Josh have built a connection in recent weeks over a shared philosophy of putting people first and building a program the right way. With Chris on board, Josh will be well supported, our coaches will be well developed and our program will continue to build the clarity and discipline required to be truly elite.

"We can't wait to welcome Chris and his wife Ursula, their daughters Jessica and Ellen and the entire Fagan family to Carlton."

...more to come.

stories.headline: North Sydney Bears royalty lands in Perth to lead new NRL club
stories.summary: Tony Rea is a man who doesn't mince his words and has been entrusted as the Perth Bears' new chief executive as the club prepares to make its NRL debut.
stories.body:
The Jillaroos are their own biggest critics after a performance that produced the biggest margin of victory in international women's rugby league history. The Australian side steamrolled through Wales in a 124-6 win on Sunday that saw winger Jaime Chapman match another record, her six-try haul equalling the mark for most tries in a game for the Jillaroos.

The toppling of Wales came on the back of a 78-0 thrashing of England and 40-0 thumping of Samoa.

But the Jillaroos are intent on dissecting what they need to improve.

The performance could absolutely have been better, winger Abbi Church insisted at training on Wednesday.

"No performance is perfect, and there's always things that we can improve on," Church said.

"What we're trying to be in this camp is to be the best.

"(We) reflect on our own performances and be quite critical and look to where we can improve individually and as a team."

Sunday's win secured Australia's in the semi-finals on Sunday against Fiji and the side aren't buying into the bookmakers belief that it'll be another walk in the park.

In their World Cup pool, Fiji pummelled Papua New Guinea 40-4 and France 54-6, after giving New Zealand a run for their money and falling short in an 18-12 loss.

Church said the Jillaroos squad watched that game with a close eye.

"We know that Fiji did put in quite a fight against New Zealand," she told the media.

"We know they're going to come out this week and we have to obviously be prepared for that".

Coach Jess Skinner believes it will be challenging to face off against a Fiji side carrying so much belief and an underdog mentality.

Fiji are a dangerous side that are quick with the ball, Skinner said after the Wales win..

"They've had an outstanding campaign, and what they did to the Kiwis put the rest of the competition on notice.

"We'll go to another level this week, do our due diligence to make sure that we're prepared best on both sides of the ball for them.''

stories.body:
The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops.

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders.

How Dybantsa will impact the Wizards on the court

After missing the first four games of the season with an ankle injury, No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa will make his regular-season debut Wednesday, ESPN's Shams Charania reported.

Dybantsa's arrival could give the Wizards one of the best starting lineups in the Eastern Conference -- which would be quite a change of pace for a team that hasn't won 20 games in a season since 2022-23. Anthony Davis has been explosive and productive through four games. Trae Young is averaging 22 points and a league-best 11 assists per game. And Kyshawn George is up to 18 PPG as he continues to make strides as an all-around NBA contributor. Add Dybantsa to that mix and there's legitimate reason for excitement in Washington.

The only downside is that Dybantsa should command plenty of playing time, which could further squeeze an overcrowded Wizards rotation. Already, 2025 first-rounder Will Riley has seen his playing time crater, but he, Tre Johnson and Bilal Coulibaly are all wings who will now likely come off the bench, yet deserve the opportunity to continue their development. -- Zach Kram

What are the Warriors' options on Porzingis?

ESPN's Anthony Slater detailed the Golden State Warriors' options regarding center Kristaps Porzingis and his lingering health issues in a report today.

[Stephen] Curry twice made sure to mention the human component, expressing sympathy for Porzingis, who has made public the lingering impact he said he still feels after contracting an upper respiratory viral illness while with the Boston Celtics two seasons ago.

"We always said availability was a big factor for our team with all the guys we have out," Curry said. "It's no secret that the [center] spot is an important one for us, especially with his skill set. It's hard to talk about without keeping the humanity of it in mind. But it is a tough one to figure out."

Team sources continue to express an extreme level of pessimism that Porzingis will ever play for the Warriors again, but he could end up helping the organization in another way, because his contract, which is only guaranteed for $3 million next season, could still prove to be valuable in executing a trade.

What Edwards' injury means for Wolves

On Monday, Anthony Edwards looked like an MVP candidate as he poured in 47 points in Cleveland. On Tuesday, that dream was dashed early, as ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Edwards will miss up to two months due to right knee surgery.

Minnesota can still contend this season, as long as Edwards returns healthy at the end of that projected time frame. The partnership of Edwards and LaMelo Ball was one of the most exciting elements of the new season, and the Timberwolves raced to a 3-1 start featuring three blowout wins, with an overtime loss to the Cavaliers marring their ledger. At the end of two more months, 52 games will remain on their schedule.

But they won't be comfortable in the meantime. The Timberwolves have a relatively shallow roster, and their bench will be stretched thin once sixth man Ayo Dosunmu moves into the starting lineup to replace Edwards. Their two-way star's absence also reduces any margin for error with the rest of the roster; Ball is notoriously injury-prone, and if both guards are ever out at the same time, a lengthy losing streak could ensue.

Ishbia on the future of NBA expansion: "Well, I'm supportive of growing the game. So I'm pro expansion.

"I don't care that it's close to Phoenix. I'm excited. I think there's abundance. There's opportunity everywhere. And I'm supportive of it."

Ishbia on the outlook of the 2026-27 NBA season: "First off, there's a lot more balance. The East definitely got stronger. The West is extremely strong. But let's put it aside.

Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

Sept. 28

Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid.

"We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day.

"He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that."

LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets. Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books.

Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade

Jayson Tatum's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate.

That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship.

"The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday. "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years."

Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team
It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch.

The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%.

Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience.

Williamson not where he wants to be
New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player.
"I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be."

Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab

Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery, Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp.

"I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly."

Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon.

It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process.

A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule.

"My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater

Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham

Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals.

Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25.

"I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed."

Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season.

"I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit.

"In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard

Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham

The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move.

Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP

At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season.

"No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said.

"The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row.

"We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward."

ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama, Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic. No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes

Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling
Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title:

"It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is."

Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures"

Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year"

During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season.

"The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder."

Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers. The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right."

Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer

Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer.

For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key.

There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract.

"I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do."

Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks

Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons"

At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense."

"I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said.

After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal.

Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset.

"This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win.

"We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi

MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes
The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon.

"It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit.

"My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood."

As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon

Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles

The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season.

Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year"

Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day.

"I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me."

Curry said knee is ready to go for the season

Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee.

"Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with."

Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions.

Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise

Members of the Denver Nuggets' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason.

"We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns."

LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks
New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20.

No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation

Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr.'s contract.

"I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that."

The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason.

Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant
Portland Trail Blazers' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday.

"Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player.

"I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent."

Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant.

Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton"

Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season.

"He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need.

"Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks."

Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season.

Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team
Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey.

"It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there."

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss
After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season
After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp
Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.
